title: Predicting the Pathogenicity of H3F3A and H3F3B Gene Variants in Cancer: An in Silico Study
content: Background: Histone H3.3 variants, encoded by the H3F3A and H3F3B genes, play a pivotal role in chromatin dynamics and gene regulation. Mutations in these genes have been implicated in various cancers, yet their precise pathogenicity remains unclear. This study employs an in silico approach to systematically evaluate the functional impact of single nucleotide variations (SNVs) in H3F3A and H3F3B and their potential association with oncogenesis. Methods: Genetic data were extracted from Ensembl, OMIM, NCBI Gene, and UniProt databases. A total of 19 SNVs from 10 transcripts of H3F3A and H3F3B were selected for analysis based on their relevance to cancer. Pathogenicity was predicted using four computational tools: SIFT, PolyPhen-2, REVEL, and MutationAssessor. Variants were assessed based on their amino acid substitutions and pathogenicity scores. Results: Regarding H3F3A, three mutations were characterized as highly pathogenic across multiple tools: rs767113562 (CAG/CAT, c.282G>T, p.Gln94His), rs1464306889 (CAG/GAG, c.256C>T, p.Gln86Glu), and rs532531600 (CTT/CGT, c.197T>G, p.Leu66Arg). These mutations exhibited deleterious scores in SIFT (≤0.01), high PolyPhen-2 scores (≥0.99), and were classified as likely disease-causing by REVEL. In H3F3B, nine mutations were predicted to be pathogenic, with rs1599343388 (CTG/CGG, c.305T>G, p.Val102Gly) showing the highest REVEL score (0.864). These mutations may disrupt histone function, altering chromatin regulation and oncogene activation. Conclusion: This study elucidates the oncogenic potential of H3F3A and H3F3B mutations, providing a foundation for their role in cancer progression. Computational predictions provide strong evidence of pathogenicity, emphasizing the need for experimental validation. Understanding these genetic alterations may facilitate the development of targeted therapeutic strategies.
